extracted.intended_audience: researchers, students, newspaper photographers/editors, and general public interested in Pulitzer Prize photography
extracted.subtask_description: Standards and procedural rules governing nomination, eligibility, categories, formats, and administration of the Pulitzer Prize for Photography (history and rules through 2003). Useful for photographers, editors, and researchers examining how photographs qualify and are judged.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nomination eligibility: publication venue
rubrics_metrics.description: For a photograph to be nominated for a Pulitzer, it must have appeared in an American daily or weekly newspaper.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is an explicit eligibility requirement — unpublished work or images appearing only online/outside American daily/weekly newspapers would not meet this nomination criterion as stated on the page.

rubrics_metrics.name: Substantive criterion: distinguished example of breaking news or feature photography
rubrics_metrics.description: The prize for photography is given for a distinguished example of breaking news or feature photography.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The award emphasizes distinction — excellence in depiction of breaking (spot) news or feature subjects. The page treats 'breaking news' and 'feature' as the substantive subject-matter axes by which photographic work is judged.

rubrics_metrics.name: Category distinction: spot news vs. feature (post-1968)
rubrics_metrics.description: The photography category was expanded to two awards in 1968, one for spot news and one for features.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: After 1968 entries/consideration are handled in two separate photography categories (spot news and feature), affecting which pool and criteria a submitted photograph competes under.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acceptable visual formats: black and white or color
rubrics_metrics.description: The prize may be awarded for photography in black and white or color.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Both B&W and color images are eligible; no restriction to a single photographic medium is indicated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acceptable submission forms: single photograph, sequence, or album
rubrics_metrics.description: The photography entry may consist of a photograph or photographs, a sequence or an album.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The prize can recognize a single image or a group/sequence/portfolio that together constitutes the distinguished example.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nomination procedure and quotas: judges, juries, and nominations
rubrics_metrics.description: Ninety judges are appointed each year to serve on twenty separate juries where they make three nominations in each of the twenty-one current categories for the Pulitzer Prizes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procedural constraint: each jury produces three nominations per category. This influences how many works advance from jury stage to Board consideration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Administration & announcement: advisory board, Columbia University, and timing
rubrics_metrics.description: An advisory board oversees the Pulitzer Prizes, with Columbia University as the administrator. Formal announcements of the Pulitzer Prizes are made each April by the president of Columbia University on the recommendation of the Pulitzer Prize Board.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This describes the governance and timing framework for awarding — who administers, who recommends, and when winners are publicly announced.

rubrics_metrics.name: No-award possibility if no nomination deemed worthy
rubrics_metrics.description: The prize has been withheld in years when the Pulitzer Board deemed no nomination worthy of the award (for example, 1946).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Board may decline to present an award in a category in a given year if it judges that none of the nominations meet the standard of worthiness.
